messages:
devon: heads-up — I'm trying to summarize a fragmentation taxonomy so we can decide when to throttle address-space allocations vs when to evict/compact. rough idea below, want quick sanity check.
ashok: 👍 send the sketch.
maria: fwiw we should include the cost model (scan/compact vs page-migrate) — those numbers drive the switch.
devon: sketch: 
1) fragmentation by extents (free-range holes) -> compaction possible but expensive across pinned pages.
2) scatter fragmentation (lots of small allocations) -> increases sg/list overhead and TLB churn.
3) address-space exhaustion (VA map full for tenant) -> can't mmap more even if physical has room.
4) residency fragmentation (enough host memory but not contiguous VRAM chunks for large tensors) -> triggers async offload.
Which of these should trigger immediate throttling (backpressure) vs soft-evict?
lisa: I like splitting reactions: immediate throttle for (3) address-space exhaustion, soft-throttle + compaction attempt for (1), prefer recompute/evict for (4) depending on latency SLO.
maria: +1 to lisa. add a metric: "scatter_ratio" = (#sg_entries / #pages) to quantify (2). high scatter_ratio -> force coalescing allocator or large-page allocation path.
nashok: Implementation notes: we can measure VA density via a bitmap per-tenant (cheap) and keep a sliding window. if density < threshold then emit THROTTLE_ADDRSPACE event.
devon: proto event names: `ADDR_DENSITY_LOW`, `SCATTER_HIGH`, `RESIDENCY_GAP`, `EXTENT_HOLES_HIGH`. handlers: throttle, attempt_compact, async_offload, recommend_quantize. thoughts?
lisa: For handlers: throttle needs to be cooperative — don't just drop requests. return 429 + Retry-After or slow-path that forces smaller batches. prefer client-visible hint so user-level schedulers can back off.
maria: compaction: we need a safepoint since some tensors are pinned by CUDA streams. heuristic: try compaction only when pinned_ratio < 0.15 and free_physical > X. otherwise, schedule async migration with prefetch.
nashok: code sketch for density calc: 
```
// per-tenant 1-bit per 64KB VA word
fn update_density(tenant, va_start, va_len) {
  bits_set = set_bitmap_range(tenant.bitmap, va_start/64KB, va_len/64KB);
  tenant.density = bits_set / tenant.bitmap_len;
}
if tenant.density < 0.35 { emit(ADDR_DENSITY_LOW) }
```
devon: sounds reasonable. what about coordination between tenants for compaction to avoid noisy neighbor thrashing?
lisa: add a global compaction budget (tokens/sec). tenants request tokens for compaction; arbiter grants based on SLA tier + historical backpressure. keep it simple initially.
maria: telemetry: we should log before/after fragmentation metrics and the latency impact. small dataset: record `pre_density`, `post_density`, `bytes_moved`, `latency_impact_ms`. helps tune thresholds.
nashok: edge case: kernel HMM and IOMMU page sizes — compaction may not reduce sg count for GPU DMA if device requires page alignment. need device-level compatibility table.
devon: noted. also need to decide whether address-space quotas are soft or hard. my vote: soft by default (throttle + hint), hard for enterprise reserved tenants.
lisa: +1. enterprise tenants get hard VA reservation (prevent other tenants stealing address-space). others on soft quotas enforced via 429s/Retry-After and adaptive queueing.
maria: one more: add a compact-on-evict policy — when running eviction, try to coalesce adjacent freed ranges into large extents to reduce future scatter. cheap ops during eviction window.
devon: can someone spin a mini RFC with this taxonomy + thresholds + telemetry fields? I'll draft but want numeric defaults: density_threshold=0.35, scatter_ratio_threshold=0.6, pinned_ratio_limit_for_compact=0.15, compaction_token_rate=5/sec.
nashok: I can stub perf counters and the bitmap implementation in a PR.
lisa: I'll write the advisory client error shape for 429 so SDKs can auto-backoff. format: `{code: 429, reason: 'addr_thresh', retry_after: 3, hint: 'try_smaller_batch'}`
oss-watcher-bot: OOM watcher detected 2 addr-violations in last 24h for tenant foo. linked thread: <https://internal/infra/1234> :warning:
devon: thanks everyone. i'll put numbers in and open RFC draft by EOD. if you disagree with thresholds call it out in the RFC.
